sources.title: Etingof, Gelaki, Nikshych, Ostrik, Tensor Categories, author final version (AMS Mathematical Surveys and Monographs 205)
sources.locator: Section 1.11 'Deligne's tensor product of locally finite abelian categories', printed pp.15-16 (Definition 1.11.1, Proposition 1.11.2 with its coalgebra-realization sketch); Section 1.8 printed pp.9-11 used only as already-published finite-category context.

contents.name: Definition 1.11.1: Deligne's tensor product C⊠D is the abelian k-linear category universal for right-exact-in-both-variables bilinear bifunctors C×D→A
Proposition 1.11.2(i): a Deligne product exists and is locally finite abelian; the proof given is explicitly a sketch via coalgebra realization (Theorem 1.9.15)
Proposition 1.11.2(ii): the Deligne product is unique up to a unique equivalence
Proposition 1.11.2(iii): for coalgebras C,D one has C⊠D = (C⊗D)-comod
contents.reason: The coalgebra realization is exactly the route the design replaces by the finite tensor-product-algebra construction; coalgebras and the realization Theorem 1.9.15 are outside this pair's scope and no item or page in the run consumes them.

contents.name: Proposition 1.11.2(iv): the universal bifunctor is exact in both variables and Hom_C(X1,Y1)⊗Hom_D(X2,Y2) ≅ Hom_{C⊠D}(X1⊠X2,Y1⊠Y2)
Proposition 1.11.2(v): any bilinear bifunctor exact in each variable induces an exact functor on the Deligne product
Section 1.8, Definitions 1.8.5 and 1.8.6 (intrinsic and module-model definitions of finite k-linear abelian categories)

sources.title: Fuchs, Schaumann, Schweigert, Eilenberg–Watts calculus for finite categories and a bimodule Radford S^4 theorem, arXiv:1612.04561v3
sources.locator: Section 2.1 'Notation and background' printed pp.5-8 ((2.1), (2.2)-(2.3), (2.6), Lemma 2.1, Lemma 2.2, Corollary 2.3); Section 2.2 printed pp.10-13 (Proposition 2.8, Corollaries 2.9-2.10, (2.32)); Sections 3.1-3.2 printed pp.14-18 (Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.2, Lemma 3.3, Proposition 3.4, Corollaries 3.5-3.7); Section 3.5 printed pp.22-24 (Definition 3.14, Lemmas 3.15-3.16, (3.56)-(3.58), Remark 3.17); Section 4 inspected only for scope.

contents.name: (2.1): Hom_A(A_X,(M_A)^*)^* ≅ Hom_k(M⊗_A A_X,k)^* ≅ M⊗_A A_X, the finite dual-tensor identification over an algebra
(2.6): every linear category is a module category over vect; the object c⊗v corepresents C⟨−,c⟩⊗_k v, so C⟨c⊗v,c'⊗v'⟩ ≅ v^*⊗_k C⟨c,c'⟩⊗_k v'
Lemma 2.1 (L1)–(L3) and (R1)–(R4): left exact ⇔ left adjoint ⇔ Hom_A(M^*,−); right exact ⇔ right adjoint ⇔ M⊗_A−, for finite-dimensional algebras
contents.reason: The algebra-level one-sided exactness classification is built in this run's finite-abelian-categories pair; the Deligne-product pair consumes only its two equivalences, through the categorical triangle of the present page.

contents.name: Lemma 2.2(i): Lex(A-mod,B-mod) ≃ (A-bimod-B)^op and Rex(A-mod,B-mod) ≃ (A-bimod-B)^op, functors corresponding to their kernels
Lemma 2.2(ii): the equivalence Lex(A-mod,A-mod) → Rex(A-mod,A-mod) maps the identity functor to ({}_AA_A)^*⊗_A−
Corollary 2.3: the (L1)–(L3) and (R1)–(R3) equivalences for linear functors between arbitrary finite linear categories, and representability into vect
contents.reason: The model-independent adjoint and representability criteria are the finite-linear-category form of the one-sided exactness classification, which this run builds in the finite-abelian-categories pair; this pair only feeds the two classification theorems into the categorical triangle.

contents.name: Proposition 2.8: the end and coend of G(m)⊗_k m^* over A-mod are G(A) and G(A^*), with explicit dinatural families, for any linear G
Corollary 2.9 (Peter–Weyl): ∫_m m⊗_k m^* ≅ A and ∫^m m⊗_k m^* ≅ A^*, the end being the regular and the coend the co-regular bimodule
(2.32) and the following paragraph: A-mod⊠mod-B ≅ A-mod⊠B^op-mod ≅ (A⊗_k B^op)-mod ≅ A-bimod-B, and the Deligne product is universal for left exact functors as well
Corollary 2.10: for every linear functor F:M→N between finite linear categories the end ∫_m F(m)⊠m and the coend ∫^m F(m)⊠m exist in N⊠M^op
Definition 3.1: the four abstract Eilenberg–Watts functors Φ^l, Φ^r, Ψ^l, Ψ^r between A^op⊠B, Lex(A,B) and Rex(A,B)
Theorem 3.2: the triangle Lex(A,B) ≃ A^op⊠B ≃ Rex(A,B) consists of quasi-inverse adjoint equivalences for finite linear categories
Lemma 3.3: Ψ^l(F) ≅ ∫^a a⊠Γ^{rl}(F)(a) and Ψ^r(G) ≅ ∫_a a⊠Γ^{lr}(G)(a)
Proposition 3.4 and (3.15)–(3.16): the opposed Hom-pairings computing A^op⊠C⟨a⊠c,Ψ^l(F)⟩ ≅ C⟨c,F(a)⟩ and the mirror statement for Ψ^r
Corollary 3.5 and (3.21)–(3.22): coend expressions for Ψ^l(F) and Ψ^r(G) in the relevant left exact functor categories
Corollary 3.6 and (3.23)–(3.24): Ψ^l(F) and Ψ^r(G) are determined by the Hom-pairings, hence by Yoneda
Corollary 3.7: composition of kernels is a categorified matrix multiplication, with coends/ends composing as balanced tensor products
Definition 3.14: the Nakayama functor N^r_X = Γ^{rl}(id_X) and its left exact analogue N^l_X = Γ^{lr}(id_X) for a finite linear category X
Lemma 3.15 with (3.54)–(3.55): N^r_X ≅ ({}_AA_A)^*⊗_A− under a module model
Lemma 3.16: N^r_X is left adjoint to N^l_X for every finite linear category X
(3.56)–(3.58): Γ^{lr}(G) ≅ Hom_A(G(A)^*,−) and Γ^{rl}(F) ≅ F(A^*)⊗_A−, the explicit Eilenberg–Watts equivalences between the Rex and Lex sides
Remark 3.17: the Nakayama functor endows X^op⊠X with a Grothendieck–Verdier structure compatible with Rex(X,X)
contents.reason: The Grothendieck–Verdier structure and its duality object are not used by any item of this pair, and the run's design excludes derived, Serre-functor and monoidal-enhancement claims beyond the finite kernel calculus.

contents.reason: The applications use Hopf-algebra and scheme-theoretic structure outside this pair's homological-algebra scope; the run's graded pair also records that it makes no Radford or derived claim here.

contents.name: Introduction (pp.1–4): classical Eilenberg–Watts statement for unital rings and the bicategorical reading; the summary relation B⊠A^op ≅ B-bimod-A
contents.reason: The classical arbitrary-ring Eilenberg–Watts theorem and its bicategorical form are authored in this run's eilenberg-watts-theorem pair; the Deligne-product pair cites the B⊠A^op≅bimodules identification only through its own finite construction.
